name: Pluto
short_description: The most famous dwarf planet, a distant, icy world in the Kuiper Belt with a heart-shaped nitrogen-ice plain and a large moon, Charon.
facts: Reclassified from 'planet' to 'dwarf planet' by the IAU in 2006 after new objects of similar size were found in the Kuiper Belt.
Located in the Kuiper Belt, a region of icy bodies beyond Neptune.
Its largest moon, Charon, is more than half Pluto's diameter — the two are sometimes called a 'double dwarf planet' system.
Tombaugh Regio, a heart-shaped bright plain of nitrogen ice, is one of its most recognizable features.
One orbit of the Sun takes about 248 Earth years.
Surface temperatures average around -225°C.

name: Eris
short_description: A distant, highly reflective dwarf planet in the scattered disk whose discovery helped trigger Pluto's reclassification.
facts: Eris is comparable in size to Pluto and is one of the most massive known dwarf planets.
Its discovery in 2005 directly prompted the IAU's 2006 definition of 'dwarf planet'.
Orbits in the scattered disk, a sparse region beyond the Kuiper Belt.
Has one known moon, Dysnomia.
One of the coldest and most distant known objects orbiting the Sun.

name: Haumea
short_description: An unusually elongated dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt, spinning so fast it has been stretched into an egg-like shape.
facts: One of the fastest rotating large bodies in the Solar System, completing a spin in under 4 hours.
Its rapid rotation has stretched it into an elongated, ellipsoidal shape.
Has a faint ring system, discovered in 2017.
Has two known moons, Hi'iaka and Namaka.

name: Makemake
short_description: A reddish, icy dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt, among the largest known objects in that region.
facts: Named after a creation deity of the Rapa Nui people of Easter Island.
One of the largest known Kuiper Belt objects after Pluto and Eris.
Has a reddish-brown surface likely coated in methane and ethane ices.
Has one known moon, informally nicknamed MK 2.

name: Ceres
short_description: The only dwarf planet located in the asteroid belt, and the largest object in that region.
facts: The largest object in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
First classified as a planet in 1801, then an asteroid, then a dwarf planet in 2006.
Bright deposits on its surface are largely sodium carbonate, likely left by evaporating salty water.
Visited and orbited by NASA's Dawn spacecraft.
